ON THE 4 th OF DECEMBER, 2025  MISC. APPEAL No. 2276 of 2025  THE ORIENTAL INSURANCE CO. LTD.
 Versus  NITIN AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Sudhir Dandwate, learned counsel for the appell  Dr. Umesh Manshore, learned counsel for the responde  Shri Ankit Chourasiya, learned counsel for the respo  ORDER
The appellant/Insurance Company has filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 31.1.2025 passed in Claim Case No.8/2023.

The challenge is to the assessment of permanent disability as tried to be demonstrated by the respondent No.1/claimant before the claims Tribunal and consequential award of Rs.3,26,500/-, which is not only on a very higher side, however, totally uncalled for in view of the fact that even involvement of the vehicle was not properly established by the claimant before the claims Tribunal.

2. Short facts of the case are that on 17.10.2022 at around 4.30 in the evening respondent No.1/claimant Nitin was coming back after purchasing crackers from Rau, District Indore by motorcycle No.MP-10-MT-8126.
When he reached in front of Silicon City, motorcycle No.MP-10-NC-6207 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35583 2 MA-2276-2025 came from front side and dashed into the motorcycle of respondent No.1.
The respondent No.1 stated in the claim petition that he was riding his motorcycle properly, however, the insured vehicle was driven in rash and negligent manner, which caused accident.
2.1 As such, the claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation.
The claims Tribunal after recording evidence concluded that the appellant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 12% as recorded in para 17 of the award.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company submits that the accident occurred on 17.10.2022 for which FIR was lodged on 23.10.2022 and there is complete absence of any explanation of such delay.
The explanation, which sought to be tendered before the Tribunal was that the claimant/respondent No.1 was taking treatment, hence he could not report the accident.

sentences.text: However, learned counsel for the appellant submits that looking to the injuries i.e. minor fracture on the front part of last toe of right leg i.e. on the proximal part of 5th metatarsal of right leg.
He submits that for this minor injury this cannot be accepted that due to treatment the FIR was lodged after seven days.
In fact the respondent No.1 has not suffered any permanent disability.
He further submits that respondent No.1 in support of his injury exhibited before the Tribunal the permanent disability certificate Ex.P/35 and lead the statement of Dr. Dinesh Thakur (AW-2).
He submits that this particular doctor is stock doctor, who appeared in most of the RTA cases and issued certificates.

He disputes the same by referring the certificate itself, which provides that on examination it was found that the respondent No.1 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35583 3 MA-2276-2025 was suffering from pain, however, in the entire certificate, it has not been mentioned that what was the disability suffered by the respondent No1.

as it is only a fracture of 5th metatarsal bone, he refers to the statement of the said doctor and submits that in cross-examination the said doctor has stated in para 3 that fracture got united fully.
He has also accepted that the claimant had come to him for getting permanent disability certificate after one and half year of his accident.
It has also been accepted by him that he has not seen the papers of the treatment of the claimant.

3.1 Learned counsel further submits that keeping the nature of injuries into mind i.e. fracture in 5th metatarsal of the right leg and the nature of work, which the respondent No.1 was and is still doing i.e. running grocery store in fact there is complete absence of any functional disability.
He submits that the Tribunal has grossly erred in awarding the compensation for non-existing permanent disability.
He further submits that in fact except the medical bills, nothing is on record regarding the treatment taken by the respondent No.1 for his injury,
The entire case is based on fabricated material and suppression of material documents.
He, thus submits that the impugned award be set aside.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.1/claimant by heavily relying on the statement of Dr. Dinesh Thakur (AW-2) has stated that doctor has clearly suggested that respondent No.1 has suffered 25% permanent disability into his right leg.
There is no reason to disbelieve the same.

He further submits that even the Police has registered an offence under Section 279, 337 and 338 of I P C , w h i c h f u r t h e r s u g g e s t s t h a t t h e r e s p o n d e n t N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2025:MPHC-IND:35583 4 MA-2276-2025 No.1 has suffered grievous injuries in the accident.
He supports the findings of the claims Tribunal.
As regards delay in lodging the FIR he submits that respondent No.1 suffered fracture, thus he could not report the accident in time.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties; perused the record.

6. From perusal of the record this Court is convinced that present is the case where the Tribunal has exercised its jurisdiction erroneously while quantifying the compensation for a minor injury sustained by the respondent No.1.

The permanent disability certificate Ex.P/35 on perusal would show that it is a vague document prepared without following any particular method of assessment,
although in the bottom of the same the method has been referred.
However, the doctor in his cross-examination has accepted that he applied a different method, than applied by the Medical Board.
He admits that he has not seen the documents regarding treatment of respondent No.1 and fracture is completely united.

He also admits that in fact the respondent No.1 came to him after one The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Nitin on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79411147/
2 and half year of the accident.

sentences.text: Considering the nature of injury i.e. minor fracture on the proximal part of 5th metatarsal of right leg of the respondent No.1, this Court is of the considered view that the compensation awarded is on very higher side.

Considering the fact that the charge-sheet has been filed in the matter and the respondent No.1 himself deposed before the Tribunal, this Court refrains from entering into the issue of involvement of insured vehicle in the accident.

As such,
considering the overall facts of the case the award passed by the claims Tribunal is modified by awarding a lumpsum amount of Rs.50,000/- to the respondent NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35583 5 MA-2276-2025 No.1/claimant.

It is made clear that the amount awarded by the Tribunal is hereby deleted in entirety and only Rs.50,000/- is awarded with an interest @ 6%
per annum from the date of filing claim application till its payment.
The same be paid out of the amount deposited by the Insurance Company pursuant to the order dated 5.8.2025 and the rest of the amount be refunded to the Insurance Company.
7. With the aforesaid direction the appeal filed by the Insurance Company is allowed in part.
(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE patil The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Nitin on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79411147/
